title: Pattern Matching in AI Compilers and Its Formalization
problem: PyPM DSL for ML graph rewriting has complex pattern matching language borrowing from logic programming (recursive, nondeterministic, constraint-checking), making the implementation difficult to understand and verify (thousands of lines of C++).
motivation: ML compiler optimization passes rely on pattern matching; formal verification is essential for correctness but lacks clear mathematical foundations.
method: Develops formal core calculus expressing PyPM pattern language semantics. Defines declarative semantics (which patterns match which terms) and algorithmic semantics (idealized interpreter). Proves equivalence between both semantics using Coq proof assistant, fully mechanized.
key_novelty: First formal verification and specification of ML compiler pattern matching language via mechanized proofs in Coq.
contributions: Formal core calculus for logic-based pattern matching
Declarative semantics for pattern matching correctness
limitations: Formalization covers core language; applicability to PyPM's full feature set not detailed.
primary_theme: Formal verification of ML pattern matching
